title: Maintenance of Adult Aedes aegypti Mosquito Colonies
author: Steven Stenhouse
materials: Place cages and any remaining materials in a freezer for at least 4 hours to ensure all remaining mosquitoes and eggs are destroyed.

steps.title: Prepare Adult Rearing Cages
steps.instruction: Prepare the required number of BugDorm-4M4545 adult rearing cages, ensuring they are clean, dry, and properly assembled.

steps.title: Dry Pupae for Weighing
steps.instruction: Remove excess surface moisture from pupae to determine individual weights.

substeps.instruction: Pour pupae through a hand sieve and dab the sieve on a microfiber cloth.
Transfer semi-dried pupae into a coffee filter and place in the lowest tray of a NESCO FD-80A food dehydrator set to 35°C for 7 minutes.
Invert the sieve and firmly tap it onto paper towels to release pupae in a single pile, flipping the pile to promote water absorption until pupae move independently.

steps.title: Calculate Mean Pupal Weight
steps.instruction: Determine the average weight per individual pupa for each sex and sorting day.

substeps.instruction: Prepare approximately 20 aliquots containing 30 pupae of the same sex from each sorting day.
Weigh each aliquot and record the total weight.
Divide the total weight by the total number of individuals to calculate the average weight.

steps.title: Aliquot and Transfer Pupae
steps.instruction: Use the calculated mean pupal weight to aliquot pupae into cages to achieve the desired population (1200 males and 3600 females).

substeps.instruction: Prepare aliquots of 1200 pupae each in deli containers filled with approximately 200 mL of water.
Group male pupae using specimens sorted on Day 1.
Prioritize female pupae collected on Day 3; supplement with Day 2 pupae if necessary.
Transfer pupae into labeled emergence containers and place them inside the cages.

steps.title: Adult Emergence
steps.instruction: Allow adults to emerge under standard insectary conditions. Remove pupal containers from the cages four days after installation once emergence is complete.

steps.title: Provide First Blood Meal
steps.instruction: On Day 7 after cage installation, provide the first blood meal using an artificial membrane feeding system.

substeps.instruction: Prepare watch glasses covered with Parafilm M containing 8 ml of defibrinated sheep blood (DSB - HemoStat Laboratories).
Place one blood-feeding device in each cage for a maximum of 24 hours.
Monitor blood temperature using an infrared thermometer to maintain it at 38 °C.
Remove the device after feeding and assess mosquito engorgement; provide an additional meal if feeding was insufficient.

steps.title: Maintain Sugar Feeders
steps.instruction: Check the sugar feeder every two days and replace it as needed.

steps.title: Prepare Oviposition Cups
steps.instruction: Construct oviposition cups for egg collection.

substeps.instruction: Cut a WypAll paper towel in half horizontally and fold one half lengthwise.
Line the inside of a 16-oz plastic cup with the folded paper so that half remains above the water line and ends overlap to form a continuous ring.
Add approximately 100 mL of tap water to the cup.
Press the paper firmly against the cup wall to eliminate gaps.

steps.title: Collect Eggs
steps.instruction: On Day 9 (two days after blood feeding), place one oviposition cup into each cage and leave for 48 hours.

substeps.instruction: Remove the oviposition cups from the cages.
Carefully remove the oviposition paper and hold it over a 5-gallon bucket liner.
Gently rinse the paper using a wash bottle filled with tap water to remove debris and dead mosquitoes.

steps.title: Process and Store Oviposition Papers
steps.instruction: Dry and archive the oviposition papers.

substeps.instruction: Place oviposition papers on a designated drying rack to air dry for approximately one week.
Transfer dry papers to labeled gallon-sized bags indicating cohort, date, and cage identification.

steps.title: Clean and Sterilize Materials
steps.instruction: Dispose of waste and clean equipment for reuse.

substeps.instruction: Place used cups and rinse materials into a bucket liner and freeze overnight to destroy remaining eggs.
Wash cages thoroughly with water and Alconox cleaning solution, rinse completely, and air dry.
Clean and thoroughly dry all other materials before reuse.

steps.title: Complete Gonotrophic Cycles
steps.instruction: Maintain three gonotrophic cycles over a three-week period, offering one blood meal per week. After all egg collection cycles are complete, remove sugar feeders and disassemble cages.

steps.title: Environmental Maintenance
steps.instruction: Maintain cages under controlled environmental conditions (temperature, humidity, and photoperiod) appropriate for Aedes aegypti to support adult survival and mating.
